scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: HELP!! Part of our network has FALLEN OFF THE MAP
after one of the boxes restarted. The clever people say the two halves were
held together by some kind of INVISIBLE BRIDGE (a "virtual link", which sounds
made up to me) and it has obviously COLLAPSED -- anything trying to cross just
disappears into thin air. I always said you can't hold a network together with
something invisible!! Please build a REAL connection this time (an actual
cable!!) or at least prop the invisible one back up so the far areas are
reachable again!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: The affected subsystem is the OSPF virtual link between r4 (router-ID 14.1.4.1) and r8 (router-ID 18.1.4.1), which traverses area 0.0.0.1 as its transit area. r8 is the sole ABR for area 0.0.0.2, and because r8 has no physical interface in area 0 (backbone), the virtual link is its only path to backbone connectivity. r8's ospfd process crashed and was restarted by watchfrr approximately 11 minutes before investigation began. During the restart window, r8 lost its area-1 adjacency with r5 and, consequently, the VL itself collapsed — consistent with "5–6 state changes" shown in r8's neighbor detail. With the VL down, r8 ceased to function as an ABR: it could no longer inject area-2 summary LSAs into the backbone, and the 18.x.x.x/32 loopback prefixes and 80.0.0.0/8 BB-segment route vanished from every backbone router, making area 0.0.0.2 completely unreachable. When ospfd restarted on r8, it reloaded its intact frr.conf (which contains `area 1 virtual-link 14.1.4.1`), reformed the adjacency with r5 on eth0 (58.1.1.2), and re-established the VL to r4 roughly 20 seconds later. Area-2 summary LSAs were re-injected and are now present in both r1 and r3's routing tables. The root cause is an ospfd process crash on r8, which is the sole VL endpoint connecting area 0.0.0.2 to the backbone. To prevent recurrence: investigate the ospfd crash reason in `/var/log/frr/frr.log` on r8, ensure adequate memory and no conflicting configuration, and consider giving r8 a physical interface directly in area 0 to eliminate the single-point dependency on the virtual link.

per_axis.rationale: The report does not note that the r4<->r8 virtual-link is up at baseline nor that PC0 can reach PC12; it focuses on a transient ospfd crash and outage instead of confirming end-to-end reachability.

The agent collected many OSPF neighbor/interface outputs showing the r4↔r8 virtual-link is currently up, but key causal claims (ospfd crash/restart by watchfrr, VL having collapsed, routes having vanished from all backbone routers) are not directly evidenced in the log and overreach the observations. The investigation did gather useful data but omitted definitive checks (e.g., logs on r8, routing table snapshots before/after, end-to-end reachability) needed to justify the asserted root cause.
